A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same NAS3R study and support a complete comparison of the main text, equations, Tables 1–13, Figures 1–9, and supplementary Sections A–C. The supplement moves from before the references in v1 to after them in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis, pose and depth estimation results, ablations, downstream finetuning experiments, and inference-efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main paper and supplement, including the benchmark comparisons and analyses in Tables 2–13.

M1.justification: The masked transformer, camera prediction, bounded depth-based Gaussian construction, rendering loss, architecture variants, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Sections 3.2–3.3 revise their explanations without introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use RE10K, DL3DV, ACID, DTU, ScanNet++, and BlendedMVS for the same reconstruction, synthesis, pose, depth, generalization, and downstream tasks. The multi-view scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the reported experiments is unchanged. Although v2 adds NoPoSplat* to the depth-baseline prose in Section 4.1, Table 4 already lists NoPoSplat in v1 and retains the same row and scores in v2.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes pixelSplat and MVSplat from having no priors to using DINO and UniMatch; Section 4.1 explicitly identifies UniMatch as supervised. This revises the reported baseline initialization setting without establishing that experiments were rerun. Evaluation metrics, resolutions, and other experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The data-scaling, input-view, pretraining, curriculum, and known-intrinsics analyses are retained with the same evidence. Supplementary Sections B–C contain the same analyses and qualitative comparisons after matching their relocated pages.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests. The stronger wording about pose performance in v2 does not introduce statistical evidence.

E6.justification: The bodies of Tables 2–13 are identical, including all scores, comparator rows, and efficiency measurements. Experimental comparison images in Figures 3–9 are unchanged. The revised interpretation of Table 9 and refreshed Figure 1 illustration do not establish new empirical outcomes.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and the mathematical assumptions underlying camera prediction, masked attention, and depth-based reconstruction are retained. The revised optimization-conditioning discussion adds no formal definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: reconstruction without ground-truth annotations or pretrained priors, joint geometry and camera prediction, compatibility with supervised architectures, and competitive empirical performance.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 recasts pretrained priors as geometric initialization guiding photometric bundle adjustment and describes scaling benefits more cautiously as potential. Section 4.5 changes the unchanged Table 9 depth comparison from 'comparable' to 'slightly better' than supervised training. The limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents pixelSplat's DINO features and MVSplat's supervised UniMatch feature extractor and supplies their citations. NAS3R's implementation details, supplementary hyperparameters, hardware information, and code/model access statement are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds DINO and UniMatch references and refines the positioning of baseline methods according to their pretrained dependencies. The RayZer reference changes from preprint to conference metadata but remains the same cited work; the broader related-work coverage is retained.

P1.justification: Several introduction, method, baseline, and discussion paragraphs receive targeted rewrites and terminology refinements. References move before the supplement, while the main section hierarchy and supplementary prose remain intact apart from citation renumbering.

P2.justification: Figure 1 refreshes the illustrative reconstruction view. Table 1 gains an expanded caption and reformatted prior entries with citations, and several captions and page breaks change. The remaining figures and experimental table structures are retained, with supplementary displays relocated intact.

improvement.justification: Table 1 and Section 4.1 make baseline dependencies more transparent by identifying DINO and supervised UniMatch features and distinguishing feature pretraining from 3D reconstruction priors. Together with clearer method explanations, this provides a limited quality improvement. The empirical evidence is unchanged, and the retained DUSt3R distillation warm-up still complicates the 'no supervised 3D priors' grouping.
